newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BREWERS COME FROM SEVEN DOWN FOR 13-11 WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BREWERS COME FROM SEVEN DOWN FOR 13-11 WIN.

text.p: The Milwaukee Brewers spotted the Boston Red Sox the first seven runs of the game before rallying for a 13-11 victory on Wednesday.

Jeromy Burnitz had a pair of doubles and three RBI and nine different players scored runs as the surging Brewers won for the sixth time in seven games to move into first place in the American League Central Division.
"I don't think anyone expected it, probably not even anybody on this team," said Burnitz of leading the division.
Jeff Cirillo also had three hits and drove in a pair of runs as the Brewers overcame a 6-0 second-inning deficit by scoring five runs in the third and eight more in the fourth.
"We erupted on them, we had a terrific inning in the fourth," said Brewers manager Phil Garner, whose team trailed 7-0 before coming to life in the bottom of the third.
Cal Eldred (6-5) won despite allowing eight runs and nine hits in five innings. Mark Brandenburg (0-1) took the loss, allowed six runs in just one-third of an inning.

Boston got a three-run homer from John Valentin and a two-run shot from Wil Cordero in a six-run second. Mo Vaughn added a solo homer in the fifth and the Red Sox scored three more times in the seventh to get within two runs.
In Cleveland, Albert Belle continued to punish his former club by driving in three runs and Jorge Fabregas had three RBI to lead the Chicago White Sox to a 9-4 win over the Indians.
Belle, who received another hostile greeting from his former fans, is 6-for-16 (.375) with three doubles, two homers and 10 RBI in four games against the Indians this season.

James Baldwin (3-7) allowed two hits and three walks with eight strikeouts in seven scoreless innings for Chicago to hand the Indians their fourth straight loss. Albie Lopez (2-4) was ripped for five runs and six hits in 4 2/3 innings.
Ray Durham had a solo homer in the eighth for Chicago. Jim Thome belted his 13th, a two-run shot in the bottom of the inning for Cleveland.
In Baltimore, Rafael Palmeiro triggered a four-run seventh inning with a two-run double as the red-hot Orioles blew a five-run lead before recovering for a 9-7 over the New York Yankees.
Pinch-hitter Charlie Hayes belted his third career grand slam off reliever Jesse Orosco (2-0) to cap a five-run seventh inning and pull the Yankees even at 5-5.
But the Orioles answered with four runs in the bottom of the inning to extend their winning streak to seven games and leave the second-placed Yankees 9 1/2 games adrift in the American League East.
Palmeiro has 21 RBI in his last 20 games.
In Anaheim, Allen Watson allowed two runs over six innings for his third straight win and Dave Hollins hit a three-run homer to lead the Angels to a 7-3 win over the Kansas City Royals.
Watson (4-3) gave up six hits, walked two and struck out eight before leaving with tightness in his left hip. In his last three starts, the left-hander has allowed three runs over 20 innings.
Glendon Rusch (3-3) was tagged for seven runs and 10 hits over 5 1/3 innings for the loss.
The Royals pulled within 3-2 with a pair of runs in the fifth inning, but the Angels scored four times in the sixth, capped by a two-run single by Tony Phillips.
